name: Apia
tagline: Samoa's easygoing capital and harbour base for Upolu's reefs, falls and history
description: Apia is Samoa's capital, on the north coast of Upolu, with about 42,000 people. It is small and a little worn, and most visitors use it to get their bearings and plan trips around the island. In town the clock tower war memorial marks the centre, and Robert Louis Stevenson's house at Vailima lies 5 km south. In 1889 seven German, American and British warships refused to leave the harbour as a typhoon approached, and all but one were lost.
whyVisit: Snorkel the reef at Palolo Deep
Base yourself for Upolu day trips

goodToKnow.title: Check the Palolo Deep tide
goodToKnow.detail: At low tide you paddle over sharp coral to reach deep water. Read the tide chart at the gate and swim out on the incoming tide.

goodToKnow.title: Sunday is a rest day
goodToKnow.detail: Most shops and businesses close and you should not walk through villages. Dress modestly, with knee-length shorts away from the beach.

goodToKnow.title: Mind dogs after dusk
goodToKnow.detail: Free-roaming dogs are common in Apia in the evening. Most ignore you, and walking in from the suburbs after dark is best avoided.

bestTimeBlurb: Apia is driest in {months}, well clear of the October to March rainy and cyclone season.

name: Savaiʻi
tagline: Samoa's quieter big island of lava fields, blowholes and village life
description: Savaiʻi is the larger and less developed of Samoa's two main islands, with no real towns, just villages strung along one well-paved road that circles the island. The coast shifts between black volcanic ash, white sand beaches and cliffs, and every few miles brings a colonial-style church. Lava fields from eruptions between 1905 and 1911 can be visited from that road, and the Pulemelei mound is the largest ancient structure in Polynesia. Many travellers call it the real Samoa.

goodToKnow.title: Plan around the ferry
goodToKnow.detail: The crossing from Mulifanua to Salelologa takes 1 hr 15 min, with up to five sailings a day from 06:00 to 16:00.

goodToKnow.title: Local licence needed
goodToKnow.detail: International licences are not accepted. A local licence costs WST 21 and lasts a month, and a car helps most on the Falealupo Peninsula.

goodToKnow.title: Expect fees and guides
goodToKnow.detail: Blowholes charge WS$5 entry, and some caves and lava sites need a village guide. Agree prices first and ignore unasked coconut-throwing shows.

bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months} for the driest weather, before the rainy and cyclone season starts in October.
